pairs.subject: concurrency-guards
pairs.evidence: src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/design/useCredentialDesignOrchestrator.ts:62 The auth-detection prefetch sets authPrefetchedRef before it starts and never resets it in this cleanup, so when design.phase moves from 'analyzing' to 'preview' the in-flight result is thrown away while the flag stays set, and the re-run effect returns early: the prefetch never runs again until resetAll, and the negotiator has to fall back to its own detect.

techniques.evidence: src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/design/useCredentialDesignOrchestrator.ts:49 Set on start and released only in resetAll (line 241), never on the effect's cancellation path. The cancelled work keeps the guard, which is the technique's "operation sometimes never runs again" failure.

src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/picker/useRecipeIndicators.ts:46 A per-effect cancellation flag is checked right before the state write, so a superseded fetch is dropped at the write site (NegotiatorPanel.tsx:41 does the same). CliConnectionPanel's runInstallCheck/runVerify have no such check, but the UI state appears to serialize them.

src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/picker/CliConnectionPanel.tsx:83 The once-only defaulting is keyed by connector label, and the comment at line 79 names the equivalence class ("once per connector") and the reason a broader key failed.

src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/picker/CliConnectionPanel.tsx:284 The second-caller policy for the CLI credential save is refuse (the control is disabled while saving), and the flag is released in finally at line 101. It is a per-instance scalar, not a shared registry.

src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/picker/useRecipeIndicators.ts:44 The module cache publishes the resolved value, not a promise. The precondition (a host that tears down continuations) does not hold in a browser JS runtime, so this is the technique's own "when not" case.

pairs.subject: concurrency-guards
pairs.evidence: src/features/shared/components/forms/DesignInput.tsx:76 handleDrop calls processFile for every dropped file, but files of type 'other' go into one scalar pendingFile slot, so a second such file overwrites the first before the user classifies it and the first is silently lost.

techniques.evidence: src/features/shared/components/forms/DesignInput.tsx:76 A scalar slot trampled by a second key (two files in one drop), which is exactly the "scalar flags do not scale past one key" failure. The slot should be keyed or queued per file.

src/features/shared/components/forms/DirectoryPickerInput.tsx:70 The browsing guard is released in finally, so success, a dismissed dialog and a thrown picker all release it, and the browse button refuses while it is held (line 114).
